findings.title: No test for a second chart load while the first is in flight (cancelInFlight)
findings.failure_scenario: Remove `cancelInFlight: true` (or the whole `.cancellable`) at AssetDetailFeature.swift:58 and every test still passes. chartFailureThenRetry lets the first request finish before it sends the retry, so the two requests never overlap. dismissCancelsChart passes through ifLet's own cancellation of the child's effects on dismiss, so it does not pin CancelID.chart. After that change, two quick retry taps would let a stale chart response overwrite a newer one. The shipped code is correct today.
findings.evidence: AssetDetailFeature.swift:58 `.cancellable(id: CancelID.chart, cancelInFlight: true)`. AssetDetailFeatureTests.swift:37-42 sends .task, receives its response, then sends .retryChartButtonTapped. No test sends .task or .retryChartButtonTapped twice while fetchChart is suspended. dismissCancelsChart (lines 47-75) dismisses through WatchlistFeature's .ifLet, which cancels the presented child's effects whatever their ids are.
findings.fix: Add a test where the first fetchChart suspends, a second .retryChartButtonTapped is sent, and only the second response is applied. Assert the first request was cancelled.
findings.verification_note: I read AssetDetailFeature.swift and all 3 detail tests. None of them overlaps 2 chart requests in the same store, so cancelInFlight goes unchecked. The dismiss test goes through the parent's ifLet, and TCA's presentation cancels the child's effects on dismiss, so that test passes even with no CancelID. The finding's mutation survives the suite. It is a test gap only: the production code cancels correctly, so this is no-harm-yet at minor. I did not open the playbook text for P9; the finding is a defect, so I checked it by tracing the code.

findings.title: Untested edges: unknown asset tap, tap with no quote, retry after a failed refresh, empty or duplicate quotes
findings.failure_scenario: Each of these changes leaves all tests green: (1) replace the guard at WatchlistFeature.swift:79 with a force unwrap; (2) set `.loading` unconditionally at line 72; (3) switch line 84 to uniqueKeysWithValues. Changes (1) and (3) would crash on input no test sends: an unknown id, or duplicate assetIDs in a response. Change (2) would show the first-load spinner over cached quotes, which the plan's scope forbids. Retry from .failed with cached quotes keeps status .failed until the response arrives, and no test pins that.
findings.evidence: WatchlistFeature.swift:72 `if state.quotes.isEmpty { state.status = .loading }`, :79 `guard let asset = ... else { return .none }`, :84 `uniquingKeysWith: { _, new in new }`. tapPresentsDetail (lines 98-108) only taps "ethereum" with its quote cached. firstLoad and failureThenRetry only send .task and .retryButtonTapped while quotes is empty. refreshUpdates and failedRefreshKeepsQuotes send only .refresh, and every stubbed response holds 3 unique quotes.
findings.fix: Add tests for assetTapped with an unknown id (no state change), assetTapped with no cached quote (detail.quote == nil), retryButtonTapped from .failed with cached quotes, and a response with duplicate assetIDs.
findings.verification_note: I traced every WatchlistFeature test against the reducer. Retry is only sent while quotes is empty, so the isEmpty guard is never exercised with cached quotes and dropping it survives. assetTapped is only sent with a known id and a cached quote. No response contains duplicate ids. The mutations survive and the gaps are real. The shipped behavior matches the plan's scope (the spinner shows only when no quotes are shown), so this is a test-coverage gap with no harm yet, at minor.

notes:
WatchlistFeature and AssetDetailFeature reducers implemented per the plan. The watchlist logs failures as .error, category "Watchlist", message "quotes request failed". Detail chart effect uses a private CancelID.chart with cancelInFlight; a CancellationError is swallowed, with no response sent. The slice gate only builds AppFeature (its tests exceed the 30s slice budget), but `swift test` passed locally with 12 tests.
